einzeiler: Exploring magical and folkloric cats of the British Isles, from myth to monster cats.
kurzfassung: The hosts explore supernatural and folkloric felines from the British Isles, drawing on Celtic and Arthurian traditions. The discussion covers tales of mystical creatures like the cat sith and cath palug, alongside historical divination rituals. Listeners learn how domestic cats and wildcats have inspired centuries of myth and monster stories.
stichpunkte: Domestic cats in Britain date back to the Roman occupation, while wildcats predate them.
The cat sith is a Scottish folkloric black cat described as large as a dog.
Historical Scottish divination rituals involved wrapping a person in an animal hide near a riverbank.
Cat torture rituals were believed to summon the King of the Cats and his feline attendants.
Irish poet William Butler Yeats collected tales involving the feline king Irosan.
Cath palug is a monster cat from Welsh triads and Arthurian literature.
Some French Arthurian romances depict King Arthur being killed by a swamp cat.
Monster cats appear in various forms across Celtic myth, ranging from house cat size to massive beasts.
